proposals.before: Xiao Duola, whose courtesy name was Ruanlan, had served as a palace attendant to the Waqaghan of the Yaolian clan.
proposals.after: Xiao Duola, whose courtesy name was Ruanlan, was a member of the Yaolian Waqaghan Palace.
proposals.reason: 遙輦窪可汗宮人 denotes membership in the Yaolian Waqaghan Palace (ordo), not personal service to a living khaghan.

proposals.before: Xiao Duola, courtesy name Ruanlan, was a palace attendant of the Waqaghan of the Yaolian clan.
proposals.after: Xiao Duola, courtesy name Ruanlan, was a person of the Yaolian Waqaghan Palace.
proposals.reason: Same institutional reading of 宮人 under the Liao palace-division system.

proposals.before: He was appointed Senior Grandfather-in-law and given charge of frontier affairs along the Shanbei Road.
proposals.after: He was appointed Daifu Changwen and given charge of frontier affairs along the Shanbei Road.
proposals.reason: 大父敞穩 is a Khitan office title (Daifu Changwen), not the English kinship phrase Senior Grandfather-in-law.

proposals.before: He was appointed Senior Grandfather-in-law and put in charge of frontier affairs on the Shanbei Road.
proposals.after: He was appointed Daifu Changwen and put in charge of frontier affairs on the Shanbei Road.
proposals.reason: Same office-title correction for 大父敞穩.

proposals.before: When Yixin falsely accused and destroyed the Crown Prince, the investigation implicated Wumei, but the emperor set him free.
proposals.after: When Yixin, serving as northern privy commissioner, falsely accused and destroyed the Crown Prince, the investigation implicated Wumei, but the emperor set him free.
proposals.reason: The office distinguishes this Yixin from the general with the same romanized name earlier in the chapter.

proposals.before: That autumn Yixin again reported that Wumei had privately discussed inner-palace affairs with Xiao Yangjiu, and Wumei was executed.
proposals.after: That autumn Yixin, serving as northern privy commissioner, again reported that Wumei had privately discussed inner-palace affairs with Xiao Yangjiu, and Wumei was executed.
proposals.reason: The office preserves the distinction while retaining the reviewed Yixin mention surface.

decisions.reason: 遙輦窪可汗宮人 marks affiliation with the Yaolian Waqaghan Palace (ordo), not service as a palace attendant to a living Waqaghan; the repair restores that institutional sense.
Same Liao palace-division reading: 宮人 here is a person of 遙輦窪可汗宮, not a personal attendant of the khaghan.
拜大父敞穩 appoints him to the Khitan office 大父敞穩 (Daifu Changwen); rendering it as the kinship phrase “Senior Grandfather-in-law” is a mistranslation.
Same office-title correction: 大父敞穩 is Daifu Changwen, not “Senior Grandfather-in-law.”
Here Yelu Yixin is the Northern Privy Commissioner, not the general with the same romanized name earlier in the chapter; the office title prevents false identification.
The repeated office title keeps the accuser distinct from the earlier Yelu Yixin without placing Chinese characters in the English translation.
